newsitem.title: UK: Union to decide Monday on BA strike action.
newsitem.headline: Union to decide Monday on BA strike action.

text.p: The T&G union and British Airways Plc cabin crew representatives will decide on Monday on what type of strike action to take after a ballot showed overwhelming support for industrial action, the T&G said on Wednesday.

"A decision will be taken on Monday afternoon on what type of strike to take. We could stop for one or two days, or indefinitely," T&G national secretary for aviation George Ryde told a news conference.
Asked about the likely impact on British Airways of strike action, T&G regional officer Eddie McDermott said: "BA would be better off trying to resolve the issue rather than turning to a scab army."
McDermott was referring to BA contingency plans to employ people to cover for employees who go on strike.
"Aviation is a highly technical industry. We anticipate that if the strike goes ahead, BA services will suffer dramatically as a result," he said.
T&G officials told the news conference that of the 8,776 staff balloted, there was a 75 percent return. They said 4,795 voted in favour of action and 1,770 against.
The long-running dispute is over pay and BA's plans for a new pay structure for cabin staff.
British Airways faces a further ballot result next Tuesday, when 9,000 ground staff vote on a separate issue over BA plans to sell off its catering unit which employs 1,200 people.
